notes.decision: ⲡⲟⲣⲟ taken as Lycopolitan writing of ⲡⲣ̄ⲣⲟ ('the king/kingship'); ϯ-ⲣ̄ⲣⲟ rendered 'gave kingship' / 'established kingship.' The verb is repeated with two complements: themselves (ⲛⲉⲩ ⲟⲩⲁⲉⲧⲟⲩ) and the aeons (ⲛ̄ⲛⲟⲩⲁⲓⲱⲛ).

Greek loanword προτομή = 'foremost cut, bust, image of the front part.' Retained as transliteration 'Protomē' rather than flattened to 'image' — the term carries the technical sense of the foremost emanation/forepart of the King of Lights, distinct from ⲡⲉⲓⲛⲉ ('likeness') and ⲙⲟⲣⲫⲏ ('form').

ⲡⲱⲕ ⲛϩⲏⲧ literally = 'expansion of heart.' Rendered 'pride-of-heart' to preserve the compound while signaling negative valence (Darkness's arrogance is destroyed). Same compound recurs in segment 16 of the Virgin of Light (positive context) — translated identically for consistency, even though the valence shifts; the Coptic uses one term.

ⲃⲓ-ⲁϩⲣⲏⲓ̈-ϩⲁ literally 'lift-up-under' — preserves vertical/burden-bearing semantics: he carries upward what is beneath. The Pillar of Glory's defining function is the upward conveyance of the light-particles.

Verb of uncertain root; taken as a bearing/supporting verb cognate with ⲛⲟⲩϥ/ⲛⲏⲩ. Rendered 'bears up' to parallel the burden-bearer (Omophoros) image and the previous line's ⲃⲓ ⲁϩⲣⲏⲓ̈. The Pillar = the great Omophoros who bears up all subordinate omophoroi.
Habitual relative: 'the one through whom they customarily give the eternal life.' Jesus the Splendor is the mediator of eternal life — passive 'is given' through him.

ⲧⲃⲓ ⲡϩⲏⲧ — 'to take/seize the heart' = to ravish, to enchant. The Virgin of Light's cosmic function is to seduce the Archons by displaying her image, making them release the captive light. 'Steals away the heart' preserves the active sense.

ⲕⲱ ⲁϩⲣⲛ̄ = 'set/place before (the face of).' ⲡⲉⲛⲉⲓⲛⲉ ('our likeness') taken as 'before our face/presence.' Jesus has placed the Mind of Light (and the apostles he fathers) in the holy Church, set before the community's likeness — i.e., where we may behold him.

Feminine 'great-one' modifying a lost feminine noun — likely ⲡⲁⲣⲑⲉⲛⲟⲥ ('maiden') by parallel with the Virgin of Light formula at L15. Note that the subject (Youth, ⲗⲓⲗⲟⲩ) is masculine but the modifier is feminine — indicating that the Youth is paired/identified with a feminine luminous figure. Left as lacuna without speculative restoration.
ⲉⲓ̈ⲥⲉⲭⲉ tentatively rendered 'gazing toward' (per accumulated vocabulary, possibly from Greek προσέχω). Two faces of the Youth direct their attention upward to the heaven he established.
'The Calling and the Hearing' — standard Manichaean technical pair (Mid. Pers. xrōštag ud padwāxtag), the two divine cries by which the soul is awakened. Capitalized as cosmic principles.

notes.decision: Direct echo of John 8:38 — Jesus's saying 'what I have seen with my Father I speak; and what you have seen with your father, you do.' The Manichaean text appropriates this as the Youth's word from the King's presence. Restoration of the bridging speech-formula in line 33 follows the editorial reconstruction.

proposed_terms.proposed_english: to give kingship / to establish as king
proposed_terms.rationale: ⲡⲟⲣⲟ as Lycopolitan writing of ⲡⲣ̄ⲣⲟ; the construction ϯ + ⲣ̄ⲣⲟ functions as a verbal idiom 'to make king / give kingship.' Distinct from ⲣ̄-ⲣ̄ⲣⲟ ('to be king/reign').

Greek loanword προτομή — technical Manichaean title for the Third Ambassador as the foremost emanation/bust-image of the King of Lights. Retained as Greek-derived term to preserve technical specificity.
Greek πρεσβευτής. The Third Messenger (tertius legatus) of Manichaean cosmology. 'Ambassador' preserves the diplomatic-envoy semantics; 'Messenger' is the more common rendering. Either works.
Confirmed via accumulated vocabulary; the Third Power called by Jesus the Splendor, identified with two faces gazing heavenward.
Verb of uncertain root, possibly cognate with ⲛⲟⲩϥ/ⲛⲏⲩ. Context (Pillar = great Omophoros over all omophoroi) requires a bearing/supporting sense. Tentative.
